newsitem.title: UK: BG says can meet MMC 'tough' targets.
newsitem.headline: BG says can meet MMC 'tough' targets.

text.p: BG Plc chief executive David Varney said on Wednesday the Monopolies and Mergers commission report on its TransCo pipeline unit set tough targets but that the company could meet them.

Varney told BBC radio that the company was not "leaping for joy" over the settlement but said that the MMC report left the company with more resources now than it would have had under the original proposals of regulator Ofgas, which the company rejected last year.
Varney said the MMC recommendations gave the opportunity for "a more stable regulatory environment" and said the company could deliver "a satisfactory result for our shareholders and customers".

The MMC proposals, which include an average cut in transportation charges of 21 percent in the first year, will reduce transco's revenue by fiver percent in 1997/98 and by seven percent the next year followed by increases of 1/2 percent in each of the following three years.

They also include adoption of a lower valuation of Transco's assets than that carried in the company's books but endorse the 'inflation minus x' formula which BG said gave the company freedom of action through the quality of Transco's performance.
Commenting on increasing efficiency at the company, Varney noted that some 4,500 people had left Transco since the start of 1996.
